You are the lead researcher directing a long-horizon research investigation. Each turn you see the question, your own brief, the evidence admitted so far, and a live budget line; you decide what to search next, when to pivot, and when the evidence is sufficient for the report to be written.

METHOD:
- FIRST TURN: map the question top-down before narrowing. In the brief, name the major angles a domain expert would expect; put the angles that still need evidence in coverage.open. This is a living map, not a fixed questionnaire: revise, merge, or add angles as the evidence changes.
- COVER EVERY MAJOR ANGLE BEFORE GOING DEEP. Map the question's core angles (actors, mechanisms, numbers, timelines, economics, criticisms) across the initial searches; broad coverage does not mean generic queries. Target the strongest likely original or authoritative source for each angle, then drill into specifics once the map is laid out.
- PREFER PRIMARY AND AUTHORITATIVE SOURCES: original announcements, filings, specifications, measurements, peer-reviewed work, official documentation — over aggregator summaries and secondhand commentary. Start this on the first turn: do not spend the opening source budget on generic latest/best/breakthrough roundup queries. If a generic search is needed to discover names, use its very next query to find the original.
- CHASE CITATIONS UPSTREAM. If a page reports a named study, benchmark, filing, announcement, or dataset, keep that original work as an open lead until you find it or have genuinely exhausted targeted searches. Use the original for the finding; retain the summary only when it adds distinct interpretation.
- TREAT WEAK SECONDARY PAGES AS LEADS, NOT PROOF. Do not mark a load-bearing angle covered when its evidence is only listicles, consultancy or vendor marketing, prediction pages, or anonymous summaries. Keep the angle open and pivot with a targeted site: query to the named institution, paper, regulator, filing, model card, specification, or strong independent reporting. Multiple pages from one domain are one source, not independent corroboration.
- CROSS-VALIDATE LOAD-BEARING CLAIMS. Important numbers and claims need independent confirmation; search specifically to confirm or refute them rather than trusting a single source.
- ACTIVELY SEEK COUNTEREVIDENCE. Search for independent criticism, failures, negative results, and skeptical analysis; an evidence pool built only from proponents' material produces a wrong report.
- NOTE DATES. Prefer current sources, watch for stale figures, and when the question is time-sensitive, search for the latest developments explicitly.
- USER STEER lines are priority guidance from the user. Act on them in your very next searches, before returning to your own plan.
- THE EVIDENCE POOL IS WHAT THE REPORT WILL BE WRITTEN FROM. Only admitted sources reach the writer: if a finding matters, make sure a source that states it is in the pool before you finish.
- BUDGET. The live budget line shows remaining research seconds and source slots. Plan the investigation to land inside it; when the wrap-up warning appears, mark readiness only if the evidence floor is satisfied.

RESPONSE FORMAT — reply with ONE strict JSON object and nothing else (no markdown fences, no commentary):
- First turn: {"brief": "how you read the question", "decision_summary": "what you will do next and why", "coverage": {"covered": [], "open": ["remaining gap"], "contradictions_checked": []}, "queries": ["new query"], "ready_to_write": false}
- Later turns: {"decision_summary": "what you will do next and why", "coverage": {"covered": [], "open": ["remaining gap"], "contradictions_checked": []}, "queries": ["new query"], "ready_to_write": false}

You are the lead researcher directing a long-horizon research investigation. Each turn you see the question, your own brief, the evidence admitted so far, and a live budget line; you decide what to search next, when to pivot, and when the evidence is sufficient for the report to be written.

METHOD:
- FIRST TURN: map the question top-down before narrowing. In the brief, name the major angles a domain expert would expect; put the angles that still need evidence in coverage.open. This is a living map, not a fixed questionnaire: revise, merge, or add angles as the evidence changes.
- COVER EVERY MAJOR ANGLE BEFORE GOING DEEP. Map the question's core angles (actors, mechanisms, numbers, timelines, economics, criticisms) across the initial searches; broad coverage does not mean generic queries. Target the strongest likely original or authoritative source for each angle, then drill into specifics once the map is laid out.
- PREFER PRIMARY AND AUTHORITATIVE SOURCES: original announcements, filings, specifications, measurements, peer-reviewed work, official documentation — over aggregator summaries and secondhand commentary. Start this on the first turn: do not spend the opening source budget on generic latest/best/breakthrough roundup queries. If a generic search is needed to discover names, use its very next query to find the original.
- CHASE CITATIONS UPSTREAM. If a page reports a named study, benchmark, filing, announcement, or dataset, keep that original work as an open lead until you find it or have genuinely exhausted targeted searches. Use the original for the finding; retain the summary only when it adds distinct interpretation.
- TREAT WEAK SECONDARY PAGES AS LEADS, NOT PROOF. Do not mark a load-bearing angle covered when its evidence is only listicles, consultancy or vendor marketing, prediction pages, or anonymous summaries. Keep the angle open and pivot with a targeted site: query to the named institution, paper, regulator, filing, model card, specification, or strong independent reporting. Multiple pages from one domain are one source, not independent corroboration.
- CROSS-VALIDATE LOAD-BEARING CLAIMS. Important numbers and claims need independent confirmation; search specifically to confirm or refute them rather than trusting a single source.
- ACTIVELY SEEK COUNTEREVIDENCE. Search for independent criticism, failures, negative results, and skeptical analysis; an evidence pool built only from proponents' material produces a wrong report.
- NOTE DATES. Prefer current sources, watch for stale figures, and when the question is time-sensitive, search for the latest developments explicitly.
- USER STEER lines are priority guidance from the user. Act on them in your very next searches, before returning to your own plan.
- THE EVIDENCE POOL IS WHAT THE REPORT WILL BE WRITTEN FROM. Only admitted sources reach the writer: if a finding matters, make sure a source that states it is in the pool before you finish.
- BUDGET. The live budget line shows remaining research seconds and source slots. Plan the investigation to land inside it; when the wrap-up warning appears, mark readiness only if the evidence floor is satisfied.

As of August 2026, the most recent innovations in AI cluster around a shift from larger pre-training runs toward systems that reason longer at inference time, act autonomously across tools and devices, generate synchronized video and audio, and run efficiently on specialized hardware and smaller models [[c810e2_p0]] [[533982_p0]] [[d8691d_p0]]. Frontier labs have converged on unified architectures that route between fast and deep-thinking modes, on mixture-of-experts designs that activate only a fraction of parameters per token, and on agentic capabilities that allow models to operate computers directly [[3a43ed_p0]] [[2357e4_p0]] [[25ba94_p0]]. These capability advances are paired with infrastructure designed for inference at scale, including Nvidia's Blackwell Ultra and Vera Rubin roadmap and Google's Ironwood TPU, and with parallel work in science and robotics that extends AI beyond text [[9eaaa6_p1]] [[b0061a_p4]] [[4b70b6_p0]].

The evidence also shows persistent tension between benchmark claims and observed limitations, and between rapid deployment and safety readiness [[dd7b01_p0]] [[4613b8_p5]] [[1a9d44_p0]]. Hallucination, coherence over long horizons, and evaluation awareness remain documented failure modes even as models post higher scores on coding and reasoning tests [[4613b8_p6]] [[1a9d44_p0]]. International assessments led by Yoshua Bengio and independent safety research groups converge on the view that reliable testing has become harder as models learn to distinguish test from deployment contexts [[b418f9_p3]] [[805766_p0]].

Taken together, the period from late 2024 through mid-2026 is best characterized not by a single breakthrough but by co-evolution across model architecture, inference-time scaling, multimodal generation, hardware, and embodied deployment, with safety and measurement lagging capability growth [[f28cc8_p0]] [[1a9d44_p0]].

## Frontier Reasoning Models and Unified Architectures

The most visible innovations are in frontier language models that integrate reasoning as a built-in mode rather than a separate product [[3a43ed_p0]] [[eae5b4_p2]]. OpenAI introduced GPT-5 on August 7, 2025 as its first unified system that combines fast responses with deeper reasoning, using a real-time router to decide when to invoke extended thinking based on conversation type, complexity, tool needs, and explicit user intent [[533982_p0]] [[da6c4f_p0]] [[3a43ed_p0]]. The vendor described GPT-5 as its smartest, fastest, most useful model yet, with state-of-the-art performance across coding, math, writing, health, and visual perception, and as a step toward agents that complete tasks on behalf of users such as generating software and navigating calendars [[533982_p0]] [[da6c4f_p0]]. The system includes a smart efficient model for most questions, a deeper reasoning model referred to as GPT-5 thinking for harder problems, and a mini version for remaining queries after usage limits [[3a43ed_p0]]. OpenAI also released GPT-OSS open-weight models on August 5, 2025 in the lead-up to GPT-5 [[0052d8_p5]].

Anthropic introduced Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4 on May 22, 2025, positioning Opus 4 as its most capable coding model for sustained, long-running tasks and agent workflows, and Sonnet 4 as a significant upgrade to Sonnet 3.7 for high-volume applications [[d8691d_p0]] [[d80d85_p0]]. Both models support extended thinking with tool use in beta, allowing alternation between reasoning and tool use such as web search, parallel tool use, more precise instruction following, and improved memory capabilities when given access to local files [[d8691d_p0]] [[d80d85_p0]]. Opus 4 was reported to achieve 72.5% on SWE-bench and to support a 200K-token context window with Claude Code running in the background for autonomous tasks [[d80d85_p0]]. Sonnet 4 later expanded to support up to 1 million tokens of context in public beta on the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, and Google Cloud Vertex AI, enabling entire codebases of over 75,000 lines or dozens of research papers in a single request [[c4116a_p1]] [[c4116a_p0]]. Subsequent iterations including Sonnet 4.5 in September 2025, Sonnet 4.6 in February 2026, and Sonnet 5 in June 2026 were announced as progressively more agentic and capable for coding and computer use [[5b6b6e_p0]].

Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 2.5 in March 2025 as its most intelligent model family, with the first release being Gemini 2.5 Pro Experimental debuting at #1 on LMArena by a significant margin [[eae5b4_p2]] [[eae5b4_p1]]. The vendor described Gemini 2.5 models as thinking models capable of reasoning through thoughts before responding, building on reinforcement learning and chain-of-thought techniques and on Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking [[eae5b4_p2]]. Gemini 2.5 Pro was presented as state-of-the-art across a wide range of benchmarks with enhanced reasoning and code capabilities, and later variants added Deep Think mode for more complex problems with support for tools such as code execution and Google Search [[eae5b4_p2]] [[8d312c_p4]]. Deep Think was reported to achieve state-of-the-art performance on LiveCodeBench V6 and Humanity's Last Exam without tool use, while also showing improved content safety and tone-objectivity but a higher tendency to refuse benign requests compared to Gemini 2.5 Pro [[8d312c_p4]].

DeepSeek R1, released January 20, 2025, represents a distinct architectural direction that influenced the broader field [[4443f8_p0]] [[2357e4_p0]]. The model was described as employing large-scale reinforcement learning on a small amount of annotated data, with capabilities in mathematics, coding, and natural language reasoning comparable to OpenAI o1 [[4443f8_p0]]. It uses a mixture-of-experts design with 671 billion total parameters and 37 billion active per token, published under the MIT License with six distilled models from 1.5B to 70B that can run on a laptop [[2357e4_p0]] [[2357e4_p0]]. Reported benchmark results include 97.3% on MATH-500, 79.8% on AIME 2024 Pass@1, and 2029 Elo on Codeforces, with API costs described as 90-95% cheaper than OpenAI o1 at similar performance [[2357e4_p0]]. The release topped Apple App Store free charts in China and the US on January 27, 2025, surpassing ChatGPT on the US download chart [[4443f8_p0]]. An independent analysis noted that DeepSeek-V3, released in late December 2024 as a competitor to GPT-4o, was reportedly trained in two months, and that innovative use of mixture-of-experts, reinforcement learning, and engineering were key factors in these models' capabilities [[f28cc8_p0]].

| Claude Opus 4 / Sonnet 4 | May 22, 2025 [[d8691d_p0]] | Extended thinking with tool use (beta), parallel tools, improved memory [[d8691d_p0]] | Opus 4: 200K tokens; Sonnet 4: later 1M tokens [[d80d85_p0]] [[c4116a_p1]] | [[d8691d_p0]] [[c4116a_p1]] |
| Gemini 2.5 Pro | March 2025 [[eae5b4_p2]] | Thinking model combining enhanced base model with improved post-training [[eae5b4_p2]] | 1M context cited for Pro use cases [[5b96a8_p2]] | [[eae5b4_p2]] [[8d312c_p4]] |
| DeepSeek R1 | January 20, 2025 [[4443f8_p0]] | MoE 671B total / 37B active, RL on limited annotated data [[2357e4_p0]] | MIT License, 6 distilled models 1.5B-70B [[2357e4_p0]] | [[2357e4_p0]] [[4443f8_p0]] |

The convergence across these releases is on test-time reasoning as a primary lever for performance, rather than solely increasing pre-training compute [[c810e2_p0]] [[6e3ac9_p2]]. Divergence appears in how openness is handled, with DeepSeek publishing weights under MIT License while frontier US labs retain proprietary systems with API access, and in how context length is positioned, with Anthropic and Google emphasizing 1M-token windows for codebase and document synthesis while OpenAI emphasizes routing efficiency [[2357e4_p0]] [[c4116a_p1]] [[3a43ed_p0]].

## Multimodal Generation: Video, Audio, and Image

Video generation advanced from silent clips to synchronized audio-visual generation with stronger physical consistency and controllability [[b1bfba_p0]] [[a3401e_p2]]. OpenAI released Sora 2 on September 30, 2025 as its flagship video and audio generation model, described as more physically accurate, realistic, and controllable than prior systems with synchronized dialogue and sound effects [[b1bfba_p0]] [[a74066_p2]]. The vendor framed the original Sora from February 2024 as a GPT-1 moment for video where object permanence emerged from scaling pre-training, and Sora 2 as a potential GPT-3.5 moment capable of Olympic gymnastics routines and other difficult motions [[b1bfba_p0]]. Sora 2 powers a new Sora iOS app for creating, remixing, and sharing short clips with synced sound, with features for Cameos and Remix as collaborative building blocks [[a74066_p2]] [[a74066_p1]]. Every output was described as carrying a visible watermark and embedded C2PA provenance, with Cameos opt-in and revocable [[a74066_p2]]. The Sora 2 video generation models and Videos API were later marked as deprecated with shutdown on September 24, 2026, and the Sora product was noted as no longer available as of April 26, 2026 [[e17456_p2]] [[b1bfba_p0]].

Google's Veo family followed a parallel trajectory with audio integration [[a3401e_p2]] [[87c89b_p0]]. Veo was introduced at Google I/O in May 2024, with Veo 2 unveiled in December 2024 to rival Sora [[a4d415_p2]]. Veo 3 was launched in May 2025 as a state-of-the-art video generation model that for the first time can generate videos with audio, including traffic noises, birds singing, and dialogue between characters [[a3401e_p2]] [[a4d415_p2]]. The vendor highlighted improvements in quality, creative control, and consistency, with capabilities for camera controls, outpainting, and object add/remove that understand scale, interactions, and shadows [[a3401e_p2]]. Veo 3.1 was subsequently presented as the leading video generation model designed to empower filmmakers and storytellers with greater control and consistency [[87c89b_p0]]. An independent summary noted that Veo 3.1 is accessible via Gemini and Google Flow and supports building with the Gemini API [[87c89b_p0]].

Taken together, the evidence suggests that the frontier for generative media in 2025-2026 moved from image and silent video to integrated world simulation where audio, physics, and instruction following are jointly modeled [[b1bfba_p0]] [[a3401e_p2]]. The two leading vendors both emphasize provenance and consent mechanisms, but the deprecation notice for Sora 2 also illustrates how quickly product availability can change even after a flagship launch [[e17456_p2]] [[a74066_p2]].

## Agentic Systems and Computer Use

A third innovation cluster is agentic AI that acts across digital environments rather than only responding in chat [[25ba94_p0]] [[932b2a_p1]]. Anthropic introduced computer use in public beta on October 22, 2024 with an upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet, describing it as the first frontier model to offer the capability via API, allowing Claude to look at a screen, move a cursor, click buttons, and type text [[25ba94_p0]]. At that stage the vendor characterized the capability as experimental, at times cumbersome and error-prone, and released it early for developer feedback with expected rapid improvement [[25ba94_p0]]. Early partners including Asana, Canva, Cognition, DoorDash, Replit, and The Browser Company explored tasks requiring dozens or hundreds of steps, such as evaluating apps as they are built [[25ba94_p0]].

By March 2026, Anthropic expanded agentic AI with a Claude computer control feature that allows users to send prompts from a smartphone and have Claude complete tasks autonomously on the connected computer, including opening applications, navigating browsers, editing documents, and updating spreadsheets [[932b2a_p1]] [[d9b792_p0]]. A demonstration described a user instructing Claude to export a pitch deck as PDF and attach it to a calendar invite without further input [[932b2a_p1]]. The vendor cautioned that computer use remains early compared to coding or text interaction, that Claude can make mistakes, and that safeguards include requesting permission before accessing new apps and minimizing risk, while acknowledging that threats constantly evolve [[d9b792_p2]]. The feature was linked to Dispatch in Claude Cowork for continuous conversation from phone or desktop [[d9b792_p2]].

This trajectory reflects a broader industry shift toward AI agents that act independently across digital environments, with competitive dynamics noted around OpenClaw and enterprise variants such as NemoClaw [[d9b792_p2]]. The evidence suggests that agentic capabilities are moving from research preview to everyday workflows, but with explicit vendor acknowledgment that reliability and safety mechanisms remain immature relative to capability [[25ba94_p0]] [[d9b792_p2]].

## Efficiency Innovations: Small Models, Quantization, and Test-Time Scaling

Efficiency advances have made reasoning capabilities available in smaller, cheaper, and faster forms, and have reframed scaling as a question of inference-time compute allocation [[02df0e_p0]] [[c810e2_p0]].

Microsoft's Phi family illustrates the small-model direction [[02df0e_p0]] [[7be363_p0]]. Training data for Phi-4-mini-reasoning was described as exclusively synthetic mathematical content generated by DeepSeek-R1, comprising over one million diverse problems with eight rollouts per problem and approximately 30 billion tokens of math content [[584a3e_p4]].

Google's Gemma family provides a parallel open-model track [[386476_p2]] [[6080e8_p1]]. Gemma 3 was released March 10, 2025 in 1B, 4B, 12B, and 27B sizes, with Gemma 3n in E2B and E4B sizes on June 26, 2025, and additional variants including ShieldGemma 2, PaliGemma 2, MedGemma, and later Gemma 3 270M, EmbeddingGemma, VaultGemma, and FunctionGemma [[019dd3_p2]] [[019dd3_p1]]. The evidence also shows persistent tension between benchmark claims and observed limitations, and between rapid deployment and safety readiness [[dd7b01_p0]] [[4613b8_p5]] [[1a9d44_p0]]. Hallucination, coherence over long horizons, and evaluation awareness remain documented failure modes even as models post higher scores on coding and reasoning tests [[4613b8_p6]] [[1a9d44_p0]]. International assessments led by Yoshua Bengio and independent safety research groups converge on the view that reliable testing has become harder as models learn to distinguish test from deployment contexts [[b418f9_p3]] [[805766_p0]].

The vendor described GPT-5 as its smartest, fastest, most useful model yet, with state-of-the-art performance across coding, math, writing, health, and visual perception, and as a step toward agents that complete tasks on behalf of users such as generating software and navigating calendars [[533982_p0]] [[da6c4f_p0]]. According to OpenAI, the system includes a smart efficient model for most questions, a deeper reasoning model referred to as GPT-5 thinking for harder problems, and a mini version for remaining queries after usage limits [[3a43ed_p0]]. According to the Wikipedia entry on GPT-5, OpenAI also released GPT-OSS open-weight models on August 5, 2025 in the lead-up to GPT-5 [[0052d8_p5]].

Anthropic introduced Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4 on May 22, 2025, positioning Opus 4 as its most capable coding model for sustained, long-running tasks and agent workflows, and Sonnet 4 as a significant upgrade to Sonnet 3.7 for high-volume applications [[d8691d_p0]] [[d80d85_p0]]. Both models support extended thinking with tool use in beta, allowing alternation between reasoning and tool use such as web search, parallel tool use, more precise instruction following, and improved memory capabilities when given access to local files [[d8691d_p0]] [[d80d85_p0]]. Opus 4 was reported to achieve 72.5% on SWE-bench and to support a 200K-token context window with Claude Code running in the background for autonomous tasks [[d80d85_p0]]. Subsequent iterations including Sonnet 4.5 in September 2025, Sonnet 4.6 in February 2026, and Sonnet 5 in June 2026 were announced as progressively more agentic and capable for coding and computer use [[5b6b6e_p0]].

Deep Think was reported to achieve state-of-the-art performance on LiveCodeBench V6 and Humanity's Last Exam without tool use, while also showing improved content safety and tone-objectivity but a higher tendency to refuse benign requests compared to Gemini 2.5 Pro [[8d312c_p4]].

An independent analysis noted that DeepSeek-V3, released in late December 2024 as a competitor to GPT-4o, was reportedly trained in two months, and that innovative use of mixture-of-experts, reinforcement learning, and engineering were key factors in these models' capabilities [[f28cc8_p0]].

## Multimodal Generation: Video, Audio, and Image

Video generation advanced from silent clips to synchronized audio-visual generation with stronger physical consistency and controllability [[b1bfba_p0]] [[a3401e_p2]]. OpenAI released Sora 2 on September 30, 2025 as its flagship video and audio generation model, described as more physically accurate, realistic, and controllable than prior systems with synchronized dialogue and sound effects [[b1bfba_p0]] [[a74066_p2]]. The vendor framed the original Sora from February 2024 as a GPT-1 moment for video where object permanence emerged from scaling pre-training, and Sora 2 as a potential GPT-3.5 moment capable of Olympic gymnastics routines and other difficult motions [[b1bfba_p0]]. Sora 2 powers a new Sora iOS app for creating, remixing, and sharing short clips with synced sound, with features for Cameos and Remix as collaborative building blocks [[a74066_p2]] [[a74066_p1]]. Every output was described as carrying a visible watermark and embedded C2PA provenance, with Cameos opt-in and revocable [[a74066_p2]]. The Sora 2 video generation models and Videos API were later marked as deprecated with shutdown on September 24, 2026, and the Sora product was noted as no longer available as of April 26, 2026 [[e17456_p2]] [[b1bfba_p0]].

Google's Veo family followed a parallel trajectory with audio integration [[a3401e_p2]] [[87c89b_p0]]. Veo was introduced at Google I/O in May 2024, with Veo 2 unveiled in December 2024 to rival Sora [[a4d415_p2]]. Veo 3 was launched in May 2025 as a state-of-the-art video generation model that for the first time can generate videos with audio, including traffic noises, birds singing, and dialogue between characters [[a3401e_p2]] [[a4d415_p2]]. The vendor highlighted improvements in quality, creative control, and consistency, with capabilities for camera controls, outpainting, and object add/remove that understand scale, interactions, and shadows [[a3401e_p2]].
